Privacy Policy — Ramp Training

Last updated: 15 September 2026

Ramp Training is designed so your training data stays on your devices. There is no Ramp account, no Ramp server, and no analytics. Nothing you enter or that the app reads is transmitted anywhere, except:

  • the workout screen you choose to show on your own Apple Watch or Apple TV (see below), and
  • optional Game Center leaderboards, which use Apple’s service (see below), and
  • a session summary you choose to copy or share yourself (see below).

What the app stores

All of the following is written to your device's local storage and nowhere else:

  • Your name, height and bodyweight entries
  • Your training history: sessions completed, exercises, sets, reps, weights used
  • Your ability estimates, attributes, level, XP and streaks
  • Your settings: equipment, units, appearance, sound preferences
  • Any discomfort you flag mid-workout: the body area and the note you write

Health data

With your permission, Ramp reads the following from Apple Health:

  • Workouts recorded by other apps and devices
  • Active energy burned, exercise minutes and step count
  • Bodyweight, lean body mass, body fat percentage and body mass index
  • VO2 max and resting heart rate
  • Sleep, which earns an XP bonus when you have rested well

This is used only to show your training in context and to set appropriate difficulty — for example, using bodyweight to judge movements where you lift yourself, and counting workouts done elsewhere toward your conditioning.

Ramp never writes to Apple Health, and never transmits health data off your device. You can revoke access at any time in the Health app under Sharing → Apps, and the rest of Ramp will continue to work.

Music

If you use the in-workout music controls, the app reads the title and artist of what is currently playing so it can display it. This is read on the device only and is never stored or transmitted by Ramp.

Apple Watch and Apple TV

Where the Ramp apps for Apple Watch or Apple TV are installed, Ramp can show the exercise in progress on your own watch or TV. Not every release includes these companions; when they are absent, nothing described here happens at all.

Only what is on the workout screen is sent: the session name, the current and next exercise, its sets, reps or time, and the clock. Your history, bodyweight, health data and profile are never sent. Buttons pressed on the watch or TV go back to your iPhone, and nothing is stored on either companion for Ramp’s own use beyond what’s needed to show the live screen.

  • Apple Watch: sent directly to the watch paired with your iPhone.
  • Apple TV: only after you turn on Show on Apple TV. The workout is sent, encrypted, to Ramp on an Apple TV on the same local network, never through a Ramp server. iOS asks for local network permission the first time.

Sharing a session summary

Ramp can put a summary of a session — the exercises, how you rated them, and any discomfort you flagged — onto your clipboard or into the iOS share sheet, so you can paste it somewhere yourself, for example into an AI assistant you already use. This only happens when you ask for it. Ramp sends it nowhere on its own: you choose the destination, and from that point the receiving app's own privacy policy governs what happens to it.

Game Center (optional)

If you use leaderboards or friends features, Ramp uses Apple Game Center. That is optional and only runs after you sign in with Game Center on your device.

When you do, Apple may receive your Game Center display name and the scores Ramp submits (for example level or streak). Ramp does not send your training history, bodyweight, health data, or profile to Game Center — only the scores for boards you use. Game Center is operated by Apple under Apple’s privacy policy; Ramp does not run a separate social server.

You can ignore Game Center entirely. The rest of Ramp works without it.

What is not collected

  • No Ramp account, email address or Ramp sign-in
  • No advertising identifiers and no tracking across apps or websites
  • No analytics, crash reporting or usage telemetry from Ramp
  • No data shared with advertisers or data brokers

Aside from optional Game Center (Apple) and the workout screen on your own Watch or TV, training data does not leave your devices.

Deleting your data

Deleting Ramp from your device permanently removes everything it has stored locally, including your training history. There is no Ramp copy on a server, so this cannot be undone. Scores already posted to Game Center remain under Apple’s Game Center until you remove them there.

Children

Ramp is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect information from them.

Not medical advice

Ramp provides general fitness information. It is not medical advice and is not a substitute for a physician, physiotherapist or qualified trainer. Consult a professional before starting a new exercise programme, and stop if you experience pain. The full fitness disclaimer, assumption of risk, and liability terms are in the Terms of Use bundled with the app.
